rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 (score 158.144) is the best raced design. Iteration 2 cut base_speed to 1.2 and scored 115.67. The oval finish rate fell from 5/20 to 0/20, and slalom progress fell from 0.11 to 0.087. Slowing down therefore did not fix the bends and hurt the oval, so H1 (speed as the main cause) is rejected. Every track still leaves the line at max_error about 0.061 to 0.063 m, with steering oscillation low (0.12 to 0.28), so the failure is early drift off the outer bends, not jitter. Change: restore base_speed to 1.6 (the best raced value) and widen the outer sensors from x = ±0.04 to x = ±0.06, keeping the inner sensors at -0.02, 0.0, +0.02 and all other fields from iteration 1. This tests H2: the outer sensors lose the tape on sharp bends, so pushing them outward lets the controller see the line earlier and turn in sooner. Expected result: fewer line_loss_events and higher progress on s-bend and slalom (target above 0.3), and the oval keeps its iteration 1 finish rate or better. Next measurements: progress, max_error and line_loss_events per track, and whether the oval still finishes near 1.87 s. If the outer sensors do not help, the next hypothesis is that kp is too low for the bend curvature (try kp 3.5), or that the sensor spacing is too coarse (add sensors at ±0.04 to make seven in total).
